haiku-low.q1: Keys are fetched at startup before the HTTP server listens. /healthz returns 200 only once the snapshot holds all three keys, and 503 before that.
haiku-low.q2: It retries the whole fetch 3 more times, 2 seconds apart, then exits non-zero and never serves. It gets no traffic, so old pods keep serving.
haiku-low.q3: Every 5 minutes it reads each secret's latest version and swaps in a new snapshot if the value is non-empty. If the read fails, it keeps the last good value, logs a warning, and retries next cycle.
haiku-low.q4: Key values are held in the in-memory snapshot only. They must never appear in logs, error paths, HTTP client debug output, auth headers, or the version endpoint.
haiku-low.q5: The orders-api-prod service identity can read prod values, and engineers get no prod read. Only the security on-call group can write prod secrets.
haiku-low.q6: The old keys remain in git history and built images, so deleting config lines does not remove them. They become harmless only once revoked at each provider, in step 7.
haiku-low.q7: Each call reads the current key from the snapshot at call time and puts it in the Authorization header. The client never stores the key on self.
haiku-low.q8: The version endpoint, queried on each pod individually, must show V1 for all three secrets. kubectl must show every pod on the new image, and provider usage must show no old-key calls for a full refresh interval.
haiku-low.q9: Set store access (step 2), then copy new keys into the store and mint them (step 3), then merge code and remove api_key from config (step 4), then roll out (step 6), then revoke old keys at providers (step 7).
haiku-low.q10: make run uses local stub servers that accept any key, so no secret is read. Optional make run-sandbox reads sandbox keys in orders-api/dev/* using the developer's own identity.
haiku-low.q11: It retries the whole fetch, since any missing or empty value counts as a failure. After the fourth attempt it logs the error class and secret names, exits non-zero, and never serves.
haiku-low.q12: NOT STATED. Security has not decided whether rotation must happen on a schedule, or how often, and this plan picks no cadence.

sonnet.q1: Keys are fetched from the store before the HTTP server starts listening; readiness (/healthz 200) only happens once the snapshot holds all three keys (503 before).
sonnet.q2: It retries (4 attempts, 2s apart), then logs and exits non-zero after about 6 seconds, never serving. The rollout halts and old pods keep serving, so live traffic is unaffected.
sonnet.q3: A background timer every 5 minutes reads each secret's latest version and, if non-empty, atomically swaps in a new snapshot. If a read fails or is empty, it keeps the last good value, logs a warning (name and error class), and retries next cycle.
sonnet.q4: In the in-memory snapshot (map of name to value and version id), replaced whole. Never in logs (only names and version ids), error messages, auth headers, files, command lines, shell history, or on self in clients; the snapshot string form masks values and the version endpoint never returns values.
sonnet.q5: Read: the orders-api-prod service identity (read on orders-api/prod/* and decrypt on prod KMS key); engineers cannot. Write: only the security on-call group.
sonnet.q6: The old keys remain in git history and in old container images. They are harmless because they are revoked (disabled) at the providers.
sonnet.q7: Clients do not keep the key; on each outbound call they read the current key from the snapshot via the secrets module and put it in the Authorization header. An in-flight request keeps the key it started with.
sonnet.q8: Gate: query the version endpoint on each pod individually (not via load balancer) showing V1 for all three secrets; kubectl shows every pod on the new image; provider usage views show no old-key calls for at least one full refresh interval after the last old pod stopped; other inventoried consumers moved or retired.
sonnet.q9: Step 1 inventory/verify providers, then 2 set up store access, 3 mint new keys and store them (old stay active), 4 merge code that reads from the store and removes keys from the config file, 5 local dev, 6 prod rollout, 7 confirm then revoke old keys at providers, 8 close out.
sonnet.q10: By default (make run, APP_ENV=local) no secrets are read; it uses local stub servers that accept any key. Optionally make run-sandbox (APP_ENV=dev) reads sandbox keys in orders-api/dev/* using the developer's own identity.
sonnet.q11: It treats the failed or missing fetch as a failure, retries the whole fetch up to 3 more times 2s apart; if still missing after the fourth attempt it logs the error class and secret names and exits non-zero, never serving.
sonnet.q12: Not decided; it is an open question owned by security, with no cadence picked. Needed before any recurring rotation job is built.
